To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

NFP and Dmi3 play a dual role during the early steps of nodules development in M. truncatula, as they are required both for the formation of nodule primordium (NFP) and for infection thread (IT) formation (DMI3).

NFP and Dmi3 are required in the epidermal layer to control infection thread formation, whereas NFP and DMi3 are required in both the epidermal and cortical cell layers to control the formation of nodule organ primordia, and that the signal controlling the activation of Dmi3 in the cortex is produced in the epidemral layer.
NFP and DDMI3 are required in different cells layers of the Medicago root for nodule organogenesis, and NFP is required in the root cortex for nodule organ formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the establishment of the symbiosis between legumes and nitrogen-fixing bacteria.
the mechanisms that control the formation of the symbiotic organ, the root nodule, during the establishment of the legume-rhizobia symbiosis.
the molecular basis of the symbiotic relationship between legume plants and soil bacteria, and in particular how the plant controls the development of the nodule organ.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epidermal NFP gene and the cortical DMI3 gene act in a coordinated manner during early steps of nodule development.
epidermal and cortical NFP and Dmi3 proteins act in a coordinated manner in controlling early steps of nodulin formation in Medicago truncata.
epidermal NFP controls the production of the signal required to induce cortical DMI3 activity, which in turn is responsible for the activation of cortical cell cycle and nodule organ formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NFP and Dmi3 are both necessary and sufficient for cortical cell divisions leading nodule organogenesis, but that NFP is only necessary and DMI3 is only sufficient for infection thread development.
NFP is required in the epidermal cell for the formation of the infection thread, whereas DMI1 is required in the cortical cell to initiate nodule development.
NFP and Dmi3 are involved in coordinating bacterial entry and noder organogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NFP and Dmi3 proteins are not only required in the epidermal cells for the formation of infection threads, but also in the cortex for the formation of nodule primordium.
epidermal and cortical functions of NFP and/or DMI3 are differentially required to control early steps of nodule organogenesis.
NFP and Dmi3 play distinct roles during the early steps of nodule organogenesis, and that epidermal NFP and cortical Dmi3 act in a coordinated manner to control nodule organogenesis.
